verdict.rationale: Brex documents an official MCP server that lets AI assistants "manage expenses", a transactions API that lists settled card transactions, an Accounting API for managing accounting data, and a Fields API for dropdown fields. Together these give an external agent a plausible read path and some write surface. Brex's own AI agents categorize spend and flag violations, but that is a first-party feature, not proof that an external agent can push coding back through the API. missing for 10: a documented filter or endpoint for uncoded transactions, documented write-back of categories or coding fields via API/MCP, an agent-submitted policy-flag mechanism, a review queue for agent-proposed coding, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can pull uncoded transactions via API or MCP, propose categorizations and policy flags, and push clean coding back for review

citations.quote: The Brex MCP server lets AI assistants interact directly with your Brex account: manage expenses, look up users, check cards, review banking transactions, track bills, and more through natural language.
This endpoint lists all settled transactions for all card accounts.
The Accounting API allows you to manage accounting data for connecting to your accounting system.
Stop waiting for people to categorize, review, or approve spend. Let AI agents do it instantly, based on your policies and with total transparency.
